text: When a trigger, nightwatch, or healer run acts with no human at the keyboard, who is the named principal: the agent, the trigger's author, or the operator who configured it?

Warren's token auth today admits any valid bearer; does 'shares' mean per-person credentials with role limits (who may dispatch, steer, merge), or one shared trust level where naming the principal is only attribution?

Commits and PRs go out under the bot or machine-account identity; must the named principal also reach Git and the forge (co-author trailer, PR body), or is it enough that warren's own events and audit log record it?
If the agent is the principal, whose limits bound a run: the agent's own grant, or the role of the person who caused it?
Does 'on the way out' mean on each outbound request (a proxy adds the key as traffic leaves the sandbox), or when the run finishes?

The harness needs a model API key to run at all: does that key count as a long-lived secret here, meaning every LLM call must route through a Warren-held proxy rather than the sandbox holding ANTHROPIC_API_KEY?

Is a short-lived, run-scoped credential (e.g. a 1-hour GitHub App installation token limited to one repo) allowed inside the sandbox, or must the agent hold zero credentials of any lifetime and leave all pushes, fetches and MCP calls to Warren?

With a single gateway proxy, the sandbox still holds a key to the gateway: must that key be minted per run and revoked at reap, so each proxied call traces to that run's named principal (r-c818), or can one shared gateway key serve all runs?

Must the gateway proxy also be the sandbox's only network egress (all three runtimes: bwrap/sandbox-exec, Docker, K8s), or is it only where credentials get attached while other outbound traffic stays open?
What is this not trying to solve?
When a GitHub label or issue triggers a run, the person who caused it may have no warren credential; is a bare GitHub login enough to name them, or must every causer map to a warren user with a role?

Audit-log is an opt-in extension outside core; does 'warren's own events and audit log record it' mean core run events must carry the principal triple, so a team without the extension still has the record?
